response.markdown_report:
**Proposed direction: precision-gated, matched-target prefix cropping.** At 10% progress, prioritize an interpretable GRU4Rec experiment before adding learned history selectors. Cropping has precedent [4–6]; the contribution is controlled identification, with no demonstrated validation gain.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Padding comparisons fail tolerance in every category, while identical repeated executions match. Numerical execution paths and semantic defects remain unresolved; cuDNN TF32 warrants controlled investigation [1,2]. The one changed ordered top-10 list does not establish changed membership or HR@10. (2) Electronics has 7.3% sampled negative-over-positive comparisons versus 1.25% for CDs_and_Vinyl. These training measurements establish neither held-out performance nor cropping benefits. (3) Feedback motivates recency hypotheses, but ownership, compatibility and immediate intent remain unobserved.

**Insights from related work.** (1) GRU biases can update states on zero inputs [1]; zero embeddings alone do not ensure padding invariance. (2) Batched and singleton computations can differ numerically [2]; localize discrepancies before repair. (3) Shuffling tests chronology dependence [3], while prefix expansion, contrastive cropping and recent-activity dropout test different interventions [4–6]. None establishes benefits from this old-prefix intervention.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Intervention | Evidence it can provide |
|---|---|---|
| Encoding reliability | Precision and padding controls | Execution-layout sensitivity, separated from semantic defects |
| Historical context | Matched-target prefix cropping | Context-policy effects under matched suffix supervision |
| Sequence dependence | Last-item-preserving shuffle | Earlier-order sensitivity, subject to distribution shift |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Precision-gated matched-target cropping: 4/7/6.** Originality: controlled combination, but established ingredients. Potential: separates confounds, but gains remain unmeasured. Difficulty: compact masking intervention, but numerical references, candidate matching and budgeting require care.
- **Last-item-preserving shuffle probe [3]: 3/6/3.** Originality: useful constrained perturbation, but established methodology. Potential: measures order sensitivity, but induces distribution shift. Difficulty: inexpensive frozen-model probe, but target alignment matters.
- **Jointly learned scalar hidden-state decay: 4/6/4.** Originality: economical adaptive forgetting, but familiar recurrent mechanisms. Potential: learns retention jointly, but may overemphasize recency. Difficulty: few parameters, but recurrence and predictor verification remain necessary.

**Selected experiment.** Resolve padding discrepancies using TF32-disabled and FP64 controls without retrospectively relaxing tolerances. Compare A, unchanged full supervision; B, full context with suffix supervision; C, cropped context with B’s exact targets and candidate pools. Keep B’s prefix gradients connected. C−B estimates this training-context intervention; B−A includes supervision weighting and any documented reduction changes. Residual dropout differences remain. Original next-item labels preserve causal alignment but do not eliminate cropped-training/full-history-inference mismatch. Deterministic truncation is a separately budgeted follow-up for stochasticity, not a silently added control.

Predeclare affordable epochs, queries and charged costs. Select one complete condition by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 and deploy one checkpoint/category. Report benchmark-specific gains, training-derived popularity/length strata, and paired user-bootstrap intervals only when individual hits are exposed [7–9]. Intervals exclude training-seed variation, candidate variation and selection optimism. No validation improvement is established.

idea.description: Evaluate stochastic removal of old prefixes in the supplied corrected GRU4Rec using a precision gate and matched-target full-context control. Each experimental condition trains one independent model per category in a separate trial; deployment selects one complete condition without combining models, checkpoints or scores. Retain the existing controlled experiment as the leading idea, with deterministic truncation reserved for a separately budgeted follow-up.
idea.motivation: The supplied measurements show repeatable but layout-dependent numerical discrepancies, including one changed ordered top-10 probe list in Industrial_and_Scientific. They do not establish padding leakage, changed top-10 membership or validation HR@10 impact. Qualitative feedback motivates testing historical-context retention, but neither immediate intent nor harmful older history is observed. A controlled cropping experiment is appropriate at 10% research progress because it preserves the backbone and separates context changes from suffix-supervision changes. Prefix expansion, contrastive cropping and recent-activity dropout provide related precedents with different objectives and intervention directions; they do not establish efficacy here. Other ideas remain useful follow-ups, but adding learned retention before resolving these measurement and experimental controls would weaken interpretation.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use the supplied corrected baseline; its implementation is not available in this writing call, so do not reconstruct its sampler, architecture or loss from assumptions. No execution or validation result is claimed. Preserve any jointly trained recent-item readout or other baseline transforms in every reference and condition.

On fixed training histories, compare aligned valid states, final features and identical candidate scores across unpadded singleton, left-padded batch, extra leading padding, permuted batch, duplicated rows, fresh-state A→B→A calls and generated-predictor paths. Use eval/no_grad, fresh recurrent states and autocast disabled. For the recorded PyTorch 2.5.1 environment, disable both torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 during diagnosis; record and restore prior settings. These controls reduce numerical differences without guaranteeing identical computations. Record device, dtype, PyTorch/CUDA/cuDNN versions and precision settings.

For unresolved discrepancies, construct an independent FP64 recurrence by promoting identical trained weights, inputs and initial states before arithmetic. Respect PyTorch gate order (r,z,n): r=sigmoid(input_r+hidden_r), z=sigmoid(input_z+hidden_z), n=tanh(input_n+r*hidden_n), h_next=(1-z)*n+z*h. Each input and hidden affine includes its corresponding bias; the reset gate multiplies the recurrent candidate affine including its bias. Handle every recurrent layer and baseline transform, and preserve hidden state at padding positions. Compare both packed and unpadded singleton computations separately against this reference. FP64 provides a diagnostic reference, not exact arithmetic or proof of semantic correctness.

Preserve the declared elementwise criterion abs(actual-reference)<=1e-5+1.3e-6*abs(reference), along with the original absolute-only 1e-5 diagnostic. Do not relax either retrospectively. Report maximum absolute error, normalized tolerance violation, first divergent valid token, repeated-run error, and discrepancies by timestep, history length and batch composition. Report score errors, top-10 membership differences and within-set ordering differences separately. Ordering changes alone cannot alter HR@10. Inspect the tenth/eleventh score gap where at least eleven candidates exist: a certified uniform absolute perturbation bound epsilon and gap greater than 2*epsilon preserve membership. Empirical maximum discrepancies are sensitivity measurements rather than universal certificates. The existing first-at-most-100-item probe is neither full-catalog evaluation nor pinned validation.

Repair padding only if a semantic defect is identified, uniformly across conditions and predictor generation. Compact real tokens chronologically before packing; never directly pack left-padded histories. Verify lengths, restored batch order, independent-example state resets, aligned B×L×H outputs, explicit empty-history handling and finite nonzero gradients. Read the greatest nonpadding index in the original sequence coordinates, never count-1. If discrepancies remain unresolved, report the confound and withhold mechanistic context attribution; do not label a tolerance failure alone a padding defect. Require finite outputs and strict training-model/predictor agreement under the declared checks before accepting deployable artifacts.

Use p=0.5 for a crop branch; for each nonempty row with n real inputs, draw retained length K uniformly from max(1,ceil(n/2)) through n inclusive, and retain the final K real positions. Singleton histories remain unchanged; the inclusive upper bound makes actual removal probability lower than 0.5. Preserve original aligned next-item labels and negatives at retained positions. Do not reconnect targets across removed positions. Unidirectional causality must prevent exposure of a position's prediction target through its input prefix. Empty rows contribute no supervised loss.

Generate crop plans with a dedicated seed-42 RNG independent of base sampling and model/dropout randomness, using stable category identifiers and explicit epoch/batch/row keys or recorded plans rather than process-randomized hashes. B and C share exact initialization, minibatch membership/order, crop plans, targets, negative candidate IDs, multiplicities, filtering, sampling corrections and optimizer schedules. Construct coupled candidate pools before applying supervision masks; keep A's pools matched wherever compatible with the actual baseline. Identical seeds alone do not guarantee these matches. Preserve B's gradient path through its full prefix; detachment would introduce another intervention. Different recurrent shapes and execution paths can produce different dropout masks, so disclose residual stochastic differences.

Preserve A's baseline reduction. Match B/C loss reductions and positionwise regularization; for an already positionwise valid-position mean, use sum(mask*loss)/sum(mask), rather than averaging masked zeros over the original tensor. Keep baseline global parameter regularization unchanged. Do not assume coupled objectives decompose into independent position losses, divide max-based losses again by negative count, or invent sampling corrections. Define identical empty-supervision handling in B/C and record skipped updates. B−A may include changed supervision weighting, gradient scale or regularization balance when reductions differ; C−B identifies the specified context-training intervention under matched retained supervision, not a causal stale-interest mechanism.

Cropping preserves temporal label alignment but changes recurrent initial context during training. Full-history inference therefore remains a train–inference context mismatch. A gain could arise from regularization, recent-transition emphasis or altered supervision weighting. If a later budgeted experiment compares stochastic cropping with deterministic recent-history truncation, predeclare how retained target positions, loss normalization, updates and context lengths are matched; otherwise explicitly report the additional differences. Frozen-model full-versus-truncated inference probes can characterize context sensitivity without additional fitted predictors. Keep them on training probes unless host-supported additional validation queries were explicitly budgeted; do not change the pinned evaluator or tune deployment truncation from these probes. Success with full-history inference supports an augmentation benefit, not elimination of context mismatch.

Predeclare common E<=200, exactly 200 batches per epoch, final-epoch checkpoint selection, a validation-query cap, precision-diagnostic stopping limits and allocations within the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-seconds. Retain the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200 despite the GRU family name; do not exceed the cap. A complete A/B/C comparison requires twelve category-condition fits across separate trials, each using one GPU and training one model per category. Four concurrent slots do not multiply the shared budget. Count diagnostics, failures and debugging against that budget. Use only host-exposed timing/accounting and supplied baseline artifacts; do not inspect other trial files or reuse their checkpoints. If a complete comparison is unaffordable, report it as incomplete rather than implying a controlled result. Do not silently add the optional deterministic condition.

Select the complete condition with highest equal-weight macro validation HR@10; exact ties prefer A, then B, then C. Do not mix category winners, average checkpoints or fuse scores. Preserve the pinned 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42. Sampled HR@10 measures this benchmark's candidate-set performance, not full-catalog HR@10; fixed candidates improve paired comparison but do not remove sampling bias.

If host-exposed per-user hits are available, use 10,000 paired within-category user-bootstrap replicates with a separate analysis-only seed-42 generator and shared user resampling indices across conditions. Compute category and equal-weight macro C−B and B−A differences and 95% percentile intervals, retaining each user's candidate set. Report hit/miss transitions where available. These intervals condition on fitted checkpoints and fixed candidates and exclude training-seed variation, candidate-resampling variation, adaptive selection bias and multiplicity adjustment. If only aggregate scores are exposed, report paired intervals as unavailable. One changed hit equals 0.5 percentage points of category HR and 0.125 percentage points of macro HR. Record all condition/query results; an ordinary bootstrap does not correct the selected winner's optimism. Final held-out claims remain the host's separate evaluation.

Predefine shortcut-audit bands using only training histories: item-frequency bands and user-history-length bands, with exact boundaries and counts recorded before condition comparisons. A reproducible descriptive choice uses training-item frequency tertiles and training-user history-length tertiles, assigns ties consistently using recorded cutoffs and keeps a separate zero-training-frequency band if needed. When the host exposes validation target identities and per-user hits, report category, band and paired-gain summaries without modifying evaluation. Otherwise mark validation strata unavailable and restrict sensitivity audits to fixed causal training-prefix/next-target pairs. Never access hidden test labels. Concentration on popular targets or particular lengths flags possible shortcuts; it does not establish causality, exposure correction or population-wide gains. Training-prefix sensitivity measurements remain distinct from held-out performance.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four routes for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts and the pinned evaluator. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), family-specific sample_batch and all ModelView interfaces: actual trained model, item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data and review_data. Accept loader tuples (None, sequence, positive, negative) with B×L tensors. Restore model mode and diagnostic precision settings even on failure. Return measured metrics and metric_definitions with counts and unsupported fields explicitly unavailable. The interpreter prompt must include measurements and definitions and distinguish observations from hypotheses.

Reconstruct the saved architecture, strictly load exactly one checkpoint/category, call eval(), and compare training-side versus generated working/predict.py preprocessing, item mappings, aligned states, final readout and scores on identical inputs. Update the embedded predictor writer whenever inference changes. Keep full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five/category, distinct from sampled validation. Use only permitted histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Reviews, ratings, item categories, prices, stores, ownership, compatibility and simulator traits are unavailable or unobserved and must not be fabricated.
idea.pseudocode:
predeclare A/B/C, p=0.5, common E<=200, 200 batches/epoch,
final-checkpoint rule, query cap, tie order A/B/C and charged budget
predefine training-only popularity/history-length audit bands
confirm affordability of all twelve category-condition fits

precision_gate(supplied_corrected_GRU4Rec):
    save model mode and precision settings
    try:
        enter eval/no_grad; disable autocast and both TF32 flags
        freeze fixed causal training probes and candidate IDs
        compare aligned states, final features and candidate scores across
        padding lengths, batch layouts, duplicates and singleton execution
        check fresh-state A->B->A calls and repeated identical execution
        compare packed and singleton paths separately with an independent
        FP64 recurrence using promoted trained weights and GRU (r,z,n) equations
        include every baseline layer and readout transform
        retain declared absolute/relative and absolute-only tolerances
        report score errors, top10 set changes and ordering changes separately
        inspect tenth/eleventh gaps; do not treat empirical errors as certificates
        if semantic defect confirmed:
            repair uniformly in baseline model and predictor writer
            compact tokens before packing; restore original position alignment
            verify final-nonpadding readout, empty rows and gradients
        if unresolved:
            report confound; withhold mechanistic context attribution
    finally:
        restore model mode and precision settings

for condition in separately_executed_affordable_trials:
    for category in required_four_categories:
        initialize supplied corrected GRU4Rec with training seed 42
        reset independent base-sampling, crop and model RNG streams
        for epoch in range(E):
            for batch_index in range(200):
                _, x, pos, neg = family_specific_sample_batch(...)
                candidates = actual_baseline_candidates_before_masking(...)
                keep = false_mask_like(x)
                for row in batch:
                    positions = chronological_nonpadding_positions(x[row])
                    n = len(positions)
                    if n == 0: continue
                    K = n
                    if dedicated_crop_rng(category, epoch, batch_index, row).coin(0.5):
                        K = uniform_integer(max(1, ceil(n/2)), n)
                    keep[row, positions[-K:]] = True
                # Reproduce exact B/C plans, samples and candidate pools.
                context = zero_removed_prefix(x, keep) if condition == C else x
                valid = actual_baseline_valid_supervision(x, pos, neg)
                mask = valid if condition == A else valid & keep
                features = model.log2feats(context)
                # Preserve B's connected prefix-to-suffix gradient paths.
                # Preserve original causal next-item labels; never reconnect targets.
                loss = baseline_loss_with_documented_mask_reduction(
                    features, pos, candidates, mask)
                handle_empty_supervision_identically_in_B_and_C()
                baseline_optimizer_step_when_supervision_exists(loss)
                log retained counts, updates, candidate summaries and charged cost
        save_final_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor()
        strictly_reload_exact_architecture_and_item_mapping()
        verify_training_model_and_generated_predictor_on_identical_inputs()
    obtain_unchanged_host_macro_validation_HR10()
    retain_per_user_hits_only_if_host_exposes_them()

report complete C-B and B-A contrasts, counts, residual stochasticity and cost
if paired_user_hits_available:
    bootstrap paired users within each category 10000 times, analysis seed 42
    report category and equal-weight macro differences and percentile intervals
else:
    mark paired intervals unavailable
report predeclared shortcut strata only where supporting data are exposed
record every trial/query; disclose candidate sampling and selection limitations
select one complete condition by macro HR10; exact ties prefer A then B then C
deploy exactly one checkpoint/category, with full permitted history
read greatest nonpadding position, never count-1
never fuse independent models, checkpoints or scores

optional_later_followup_only_if_separately_budgeted:
    predeclare deterministic-truncation comparison and matching rules
    distinguish context-length effects, stochasticity and supervision differences
    use frozen training-prefix sensitivity probes without adding predictors
    do not claim full-history inference eliminates cropped-training mismatch

originality.positive: Combines numerical localization, matched candidate pools and connected-gradient suffix controls to make a familiar context intervention more interpretable.
originality.negative: Cropping, recurrent augmentation, padding controls and matched ablations have established precedents; the contribution is experimental identification rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: Can establish a reliable basis for later adaptive forgetting within one GRU network and clarify whether context intervention deserves further investment.
future_potential.negative: Benefits remain unmeasured; stochasticity, supervision weighting, sampled evaluation and single-seed selection limit broader mechanistic and generalization claims.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the backbone and baseline scoring objective, with compact input and supervision masks as the main training changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Independent multilayer numerical references, exact candidate matching, objective-specific reductions, reproducible RNG streams, budget controls and embedded predictor consistency make the complete protocol more demanding than the earlier score of 5 suggested.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Specifies recurrent gate equations needed for an explicit trained-weight reference.
The equations show why zero-valued padded inputs do not guarantee inert hidden states.
Defines the reset-gate placement needed to match PyTorch's recurrent candidate affine, including its bias.
limitations: Does not establish that the supplied corrected baseline has a padding defect.
Does not provide evidence that prefix cropping improves recommendation.
Implementation details should be checked against the installed PyTorch 2.5.1 version rather than assuming the main documentation is version-identical.

related_work.title: PyTorch numerical accuracy
contributions: Explains numerical differences between batched and sliced computations and precision-dependent execution.
Supports interpreting tolerance failures through controlled numerical comparisons.
Motivates disabling both cuDNN and matrix-multiplication TF32 during the recorded environment's diagnostic checks without expecting bitwise equivalence.
limitations: Provides no universal GRU error tolerance.
Numerical agreement alone does not validate preprocessing, causal alignment or recommendation quality.
FP64 references and empirical score errors do not constitute exact arithmetic or universal stability certificates.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential? (2024)
contributions: Uses sequence shuffling to investigate sequential dependence across recommendation datasets.
Motivates testing order sensitivity separately from historical-context retention.
limitations: Its findings do not establish the behavior of these four pinned Amazon tasks.
Shuffling sensitivity does not identify immediate user intent or prove that older context is harmful.
A last-item-preserving shuffle is a proposed constrained diagnostic here, not an efficacy result established by this citation.

related_work.title: Improved Recurrent Neural Networks for Session-based Recommendations — Tan et al. (2016)
contributions: Provides recurrent-recommender augmentation precedent through session prefixes paired with their immediately following items.
Clarifies that changing prediction endpoints differs from deleting the oldest context while retaining original suffix supervision.
limitations: Prefix expansion retains the original beginning of each prefix.
Does not directly establish the benefit of the proposed matched-target old-prefix removal in the supplied GRU4Rec.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation — CL4SRec
contributions: Uses contiguous subsequence cropping as contrastive views alongside next-item prediction.
Establishes that sequence cropping is an existing augmentation technique rather than a novel ingredient of this proposal.
limitations: Its contrastive objective and architecture differ from this controlled GRU4Rec experiment.
Does not isolate old-prefix removal under matched suffix supervision and candidate pools.

related_work.title: Recency Dropout
contributions: Provides recurrent-specific evidence for history augmentation.
Removes recent activities to encourage reliance on older interests, illustrating that augmentation direction changes the hypothesis.
limitations: Its deletion direction is opposite to the proposed old-prefix removal.
Supports augmentation as a research direction rather than demonstrating that this intervention improves long-term modeling.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog model comparisons.
Supports describing pinned HR@10 findings as candidate-set benchmark results.
limitations: Does not justify changing the host's fixed evaluator.
Fixed candidates improve paired comparability but do not remove sampling bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection bias caused by optimizing noisy validation criteria.
Motivates recording all queries, limiting adaptive selection and distinguishing exploratory intervals from final held-out evidence.
limitations: Ordinary paired bootstrap intervals do not correct selected-winner optimism.
The proposed fixed-seed experiment does not estimate training-seed variability.

related_work.title: Offline Evaluation Challenges
contributions: Provides context for interpreting offline recommendation results under logged-data and exposure limitations.
Motivates descriptive popularity and history-length audits alongside aggregate metrics.
limitations: Stratified performance differences do not establish causal shortcut use or remove exposure bias.
Training-only strata and sensitivity probes cannot replace the pinned validation criterion.

related_work.title: PyTorch 2.5.1 CUDA guidance
contributions: Provides version-pinned guidance for the CUDA precision controls relevant to the recorded environment.
Supports explicitly controlling cuDNN and matrix-multiplication TF32 during numerical diagnosis.
limitations: Disabling TF32 does not guarantee equality between different execution paths.
Diagnostic precision controls do not independently establish model correctness.

related_work.title: PyTorch 2.5.1 recurrent-module implementation
contributions: Provides a version-pinned reference for GRU equations and recurrent-module behavior.
Supports checking gate ordering, packed-sequence handling and reference implementation assumptions.
limitations: Does not expose every backend numerical execution detail.
An explicit recurrence must additionally reproduce the supplied model's transforms, layers and readout.

related_work.title: PyTorch saving and loading models
contributions: Supports reconstructing the trained architecture, loading saved parameters and entering evaluation mode.
Motivates strict checkpoint loading and training-side versus generated-predictor comparisons.
limitations: Successful parameter loading alone does not verify identical item mappings, preprocessing or causal readout.
Predictor consistency requires explicit identical-input feature and score checks.
